acquisition.citation: Pesaresi, M. and Politis, P. (2023) GHS-BUILT-H R2023A: GHS building height, derived from AW3D30, SRTM30, and Sentinel-2 composite (2018). European Commission, Joint Research Centre.
acquisition.tile_derivation_note: Empirically verified via GDAL /vsizip/vsicurl/ remote header reads before download; see script docstring and audit_report.md. Two prior automated guesses (R3/R4 x C20/C21) were WRONG (covered Scandinavia) and were rejected before any bulk download was attempted.
acquisition.asset_id_finding: The codebase's hard-coded Earth Engine asset ID for AGBH (JRC/GHSL/P2023A/GHS_BUILT_H_AGBH, in scripts/01_download_data/download_ghsl_gee.py) does not exist on Earth Engine. The actual EE asset (JRC/GHSL/P2023A/GHS_BUILT_H/2018) exposes ONLY ANBH. AGBH was therefore acquired directly from JRC's own distribution server instead of via Earth Engine.
acquisition.old_file_finding: 02_processed_data/ghsl_layers/ghsl_height_grid_500m.parquet and height_typology_grid_500m.parquet (used throughout Paper 2 v2) have no producer script and no processing_log.csv entry anywhere in the codebase. Their stats (mean 0.163 m, max 8.13 m) are close to the newly verified AGBH (mean 0.163 m over the same footprint sample -- see 'aggregation' below), suggesting the old file was probably genuine AGBH, but its exact processing chain remains unverifiable, which is why v3 does not reuse it.

anbh_quantization_spike.finding: ANBH pixel values show a massive, non-physical concentration at approximately 2.50-2.55 m, consistent with a hard-coded fallback/prior value in GHSL's height retrieval model for low-confidence (sparse/small-structure) pixels, not a genuine physical clustering of building heights.

aggregation.nodata_cells_explanation: All are boundary-clip slivers: median polygon area ~91,000x smaller than a typical 500 m cell, left over from clipping the national grid to Ghana's coastline/border in scripts/03_prepare_grids.py. gdal_rasterize's pixel-center convention assigns no 100 m pixel to a sliver thinner than one pixel width. Correctly encoded as NaN, not 0.
aggregation.v2_bug_regression_check: v2's 'implied height' (AGBH / current V3 coverage) reached outliers up to 263 m from a double-division error. v3's correctly-derived cell_anbh_derived_m maxes out at 21.0 m -- no comparable outlier tail.

cross_dataset_mismatch_direction_A_v3_no.description: V3 footprint present, GHSL built_fraction <= 0 (>0 threshold)
cross_dataset_mismatch_direction_A_v3_no.interpretation: Median building_count of 1 (vs 4 for the footprint sample overall) is consistent with sparse, isolated, or recently built (2018-2023 gap, since V3 is a ~2023 snapshot and this GHSL epoch is 2018) small structures below GHSL's 100 m pixel detection floor.

cross_dataset_mismatch_direction_B_ghsl_.description: GHSL built_fraction > 0, V3 detects no footprint
cross_dataset_mismatch_direction_B_ghsl_.interpretation: This group's built_fraction is roughly 40x smaller than the '>0' sample average, indicating these are overwhelmingly near-zero noise-floor values in the GHSL signal (estimation noise, partial-pixel edge effects, or non-building surface texture), not genuine buildings V3 missed. This is why the '>0' threshold alone is not a reliable valid-height sample definition and the full sensitivity sweep (0.005-0.05) is reported rather than relying on it.

max_vs_p99_robustness_check.finding: anbh_derived_max is identical (21.0092 m) at every built-fraction threshold from >0 through >=0.05, i.e. built-fraction thresholding does not filter the cell(s) producing it, while anbh_derived_p99 is stable and much lower (8.21-10.69 m across the same thresholds). The max is therefore not a robust ceiling statistic; the manuscript reports p99 instead (Section 5.1).

source_cell_pixel_inspection.method: Raw 100 m AGBH/ANBH pixels queried directly from agbh_2018_v3.tif / anbh_2018_v3.tif via gdal_translate -projwin around the cell centroid (ad hoc investigation, not a scripted pipeline step).
source_cell_pixel_inspection.note: A small, adjacent-pixel block (not a single-pixel spike) shows genuinely elevated raw AGBH (up to 11.2 m) and ANBH (up to 26.5 m) values, concentrated over a small fraction of the cell -- consistent with either a real small tall structure or shoreline/water-adjacent retrieval noise (the cell sits at the edge of the generous Lake Volta bounding envelope used for this check); not distinguishable from this data alone. 8 of 177 cells nationally with derived ANBH > 12 m fall within a generous Lake Volta bounding envelope (lon -0.35 to 0.55, lat 6.15 to 8.65); most extreme cells elsewhere (e.g. near Obuasi, Tarkwa/Prestea) have much higher built fraction (8-51%) and plausibly reflect real mining/industrial infrastructure.

predictors_excluded_and_why.population_density: WorldPop 2020 postdates the 2018 AGBH/ANBH epoch by two years -- excluded from the primary sequence on the same no-post-outcome-leakage logic Requirement 6 applies to the growth predictors, not held to a looser standard.

models_primary.self_correction_note: The spatial-residual Moran's I was initially computed on spreg.GM_Error's .u attribute (plain, unfiltered residual), not .e_filtered (the spatially filtered residual the estimator actually targets), per the library's own docstring. This produced a materially wrong finding (spatial correction appearing not to help, or to hurt, in all six model/outcome combinations). Corrected to use e_filtered; spatial residual Moran's I is now near-zero for ANBH (-0.026 to -0.013) and substantially reduced for AGBH (0.796->0.025 in the simplest model).

agbh_confound_finding.description: The AGBH-vs-ANBH comparisons in the typology (Section 5.5) and regression (Section 5.2) are not independent of the retrieval-floor claim they were cited as evidence for, because AGBH = ANBH x built_fraction_2018, and built_fraction_2018 correlates strongly with the built-coverage variables used elsewhere in the paper. Flagged by external technical review, verified directly against the n=296,668 sample before any manuscript text was changed.
agbh_confound_finding.implication: AGBHs higher typology diagonal concordance (89.8% vs 64.2%) and higher regression R2 (0.946 vs 0.235) are each partly mechanical (AGBH shares information with the variable it is compared/regressed against), not purely evidence of ANBHs retrieval floor. Unconfounded evidence for the retrieval floor: the pixel-level histogram (Section 5.1) and the near-flat median ANBH across typology classes (Section 5.5), both properties of ANBH alone. The cross-dataset correlation gap vs Open Buildings V3 (Section 5.6) also does not share this construction.
agbh_confound_finding.fix_applied: Section 5.2, Section 5.5 (both paragraphs), Section 6.4 (new Limitation 2), Abstract, and paper2_response_to_reviewers_v3.md all restate this explicitly. No computed statistics changed -- this is a correction to interpretation/independence claims, not to the underlying numbers.

queen_component_investigation.interpretation: Attaching a nearest neighbour to each Queen island does not produce a connected graph (10,512 components remain). One giant component covers 42% of the sample -- plausibly Ghana's main contiguous metro/peri-urban corridors -- while the remainder is genuinely dispersed built environment (isolated compounds, small rural centres), not a processing artefact.

weights_diagnostics.robustness_conclusion: Pseudo-R2 (0.2330-0.2336), coefficients, and near-zero spatial-filtered residual Moran's I are stable across Queen, Queen+KNN1-islands, and KNN-8 specifications. The substantive conclusions of the primary model do not depend on the specific spatial weights definition.

construction.tie_rule: cells exactly equal to a median are assigned to the LOW class on that axis

typology.horizontal_axis: growth_1975_2015 = built_coverage_2015 - built_coverage_1975 (truncated at last pre-2018 epoch, replacing v2's leaky 1975-2020 window)
typology.agbh_matched_comparison_note: Same sample (n=296,668), same horizontal axis (growth_1975_2015), same tie rule -- ONLY the vertical variable changes (AGBH swapped for ANBH). This isolates the ANBH retrieval-floor effect from the choice of horizontal axis or sample: median diagonal drops from 89.8% (AGBH) to 64.2% (ANBH); tertile diagonal drops from 79.5% to 43.2%.
typology.weak_association_finding: Diagonal dominance (64.2% median, 43.2% tertile) is much weaker than the earlier AGBH-based typology's 87.5% median diagonal. Median ANBH is nearly identical across all four classes (2.39-2.52 m), consistent with the ~2.5 m GHSL retrieval-floor quantization found in script 02 -- only the mean differentiates classes clearly. Height (ANBH) is a structurally noisier, more floor-dominated measure than volumetric density (AGBH) for distinguishing growth pathways.

predictor_profile_reviewer2_major6.description: Section 4.7 regression predictors (built_coverage_2010, growth_1975_2010, growth_2010_2015, distance_to_nearest_cbd_m), by typology class -- added in response to a gap flagged in paper2_response_to_reviewers_v3.md (Reviewer #2, Major 6): this comparison existed in the prior AGBH-based revision but had not been carried into the ANBH-based rebuild.
predictor_profile_reviewer2_major6.headline_finding: High height / High prior expansion cells have built_coverage_2010 roughly 4-40x every other class (0.0534 vs 0.0002-0.0141) and the shortest mean distance to the nearest CBD (61.9 km vs 70.2-75.0 km), on predictors the typology was not constructed from -- an independent check that the classification captures a real pattern.

table6_not_independent.description: Table 6 (Section 4.7 predictors by typology class) was originally described as an independent check on the typology. growth_1975_2010 + growth_2010_2015 sum EXACTLY to growth_1975_2015 (the typology horizontal axis) by construction -- not independent, arithmetically part of it. built_coverage_2010 correlates r=0.97 with 2018 built fraction (see agbh_confound_finding above) -- also not a clean independent check. Only distance_to_nearest_cbd_m is genuinely external to the typology construction.
table6_not_independent.fix_applied: Reframed as a descriptive class profile; independence claim removed except for CBD distance specifically (Section 5.5).

validation.part_a_interpretation: High-height typology share is 90.5% in the metro core (Accra-Tema, Kumasi) vs 57-63% in peri-urban/secondary tiers, matching independent geographic knowledge not used in constructing ANBH -- a genuine plausibility check, not a tautology.
validation.part_b_interpretation: All 6 correlations positive and significant (p<0.001). AGBH's rank correlations with independent V3-derived building-size metrics (up to Spearman 0.66) are consistently stronger than ANBH's (up to 0.38) -- a third independent line of evidence, alongside the script 02 quantization histogram and script 06 typology diagonal-dominance finding, that ANBH is a noisier vertical-intensity signal than AGBH.

part_c_manual_validation_sample.note: Infrastructure for manual validation (stratified sample + coding template with GHSL values pre-filled); not itself completed field validation.

illustrative_satellite_check_6_cells.description: A small, non-random illustration of the 120-cell manual-validation infrastructure, done in response to external review flagging that no validation had actually been completed. Not a substitute for the full protocol -- see caveats below.
illustrative_satellite_check_6_cells.method: For each of the 3 region tiers (Metro_core, Periurban_corridor, Secondary_city), the single cell with the highest cell_anbh_derived_m (within the HighANBH stratum) and the single cell with the lowest (within the LowANBH stratum) were located via lat/lon centroid and viewed in Google Maps satellite imagery.

cells_checked.observation: Dense administrative/government core: Accra Metropolitan Assembly, ministry buildings, Ghana Revenue Authority HQ. Consistent with High height / High prior expansion.
Forested/rural land on Kumasi periphery, a handful of small scattered structures visible. Consistent with Low height / Low prior expansion.

Dense peri-urban residential/commercial settlement (Kasoa-Ofaakor), predominantly low-rise. Consistent with High height / High prior expansion, though visually low-rise rather than tall -- appropriately, since High is relative to other peri-urban cells, not to the metro core.
Farmland, no visible structures in frame. Consistent with Low height / Low prior expansion.
Dense institutional campus (Takoradi Technical University and surrounding hostels/services). Consistent with High height / High prior expansion.
Dense forest, no visible structures. Consistent with Low height / Low prior expansion.

illustrative_satellite_check_6_cells.result: 6 of 6 cells show the expected pattern (face validity holds for the most extreme, most confident classification cases).
caveats: Non-random: deliberately picked the most extreme cell per stratum, not a random draw -- says nothing about accuracy in the moderate/ambiguous cases where classification error actually matters.

Overhead-only imagery cannot distinguish a genuinely tall building from many low-rise buildings packed densely together, i.e. cannot independently verify the AGBH/ANBH distinction this paper is about.
No shadow-length, oblique, or street-level imagery was used, so no storey count or height estimate was attempted -- only a coarse built-density/land-use impression.
114 of the 120-cell sample and the storey-count coding field remain uncompleted.

moran_diagnostics.interpretation: Every Moran's I has pseudo p = 0.001 (the floor for 999 permutations). Spatially filtered residual I for the ANBH models (-0.026 to -0.013) is small but statistically non-zero at n=296,668 (z = -10.2 for Model C): mild over-correction, not zero residual dependence (manuscript Table A3, Section 5.3).

figures.note: Manuscript figures (script 08) are visualization/support only, not one of the 15 numbered requirements.

reproducibility_deposit_expansion.description: The GitHub deposit (github.com/dzimike/Urban-growth-pathways-) was expanded to include the upstream pipeline (scripts/01_setup_project.py through scripts/09_aggregate_to_grid.py, plus 03b_generate_250m_grid.py, and environment.yml), previously described in words only, not deposited.
checks_performed_before_deposit: Grepped all 10 scripts for api_key/secret/password/token/credential/access_key patterns -- none found.
Grepped for hard-coded /Users/... absolute paths -- none found (all use config.py, same pattern as scripts/revision_v3/).

Confirmed no Earth Engine authentication calls (import ee / ee.Initialize / ee.Authenticate) in any of the 10 scripts, despite environment.yml declaring earthengine-api as a project dependency for other, non-deposited parts of the wider project.

still_not_reproducible_without: The raw third-party datasets (GHSL, Open Buildings V3/2.5D Temporal, Overture, OSM, WorldPop, Ghana PHC, GADM, DEM/terrain, night-lights) -- licensing prevents redistribution.

A working install of the upstream conda environment (environment.yml, python=3.11 with rasterio/fiona/full GDAL bindings) -- not re-verified in the environment this v3 revision was prepared in, which lacks system GDAL/rasterio (see pixel_validation/aggregation notes elsewhere in this file and audit_report.md Section 6).
